## Lead Rescue wait sweep
n8n owns scheduling only: fire on an interval and call the application's existing full-sweep endpoint (no `incidentId` in the body). Every eligibility, idempotency, claim, and escalation decision happens inside `checkAllWaitingIncidents`/`checkWaitIncident` — unmodified by this workflow. No IF/Switch node exists here because this graph never asks a business question; it only asks the clock.

Worst-case sweep execution time is expected to stay far under the 1-minute interval (a handful of file reads/writes per waiting incident), so overlapping executions are possible in principle but never unsafe: `OperationClaimStore`'s cross-process-exclusive claim already makes two overlapping sweeps (or a genuinely concurrent one from a second n8n instance) resolve any given incident's effect at most once. No scheduler-level mutex or lock was added — that guarantee already existed and is proven directly by `tests/lead-rescue-wait-sweep.test.ts`.

Set 'Sweep Waiting Incidents' -> URL to wherever the Lead Rescue app is actually reachable (e.g. http://host.docker.internal:<port>/api/lead-rescue/wait-incidents/check for a local Docker n8n instance talking to a local Next.js dev server). The 1-minute interval is a demo-appropriate cadence, not a production SLA decision — see docs/STATUS.md.
